item.title: JavaScript Canvas Drawing to Server: Base64 vs Blob Upload Methods
item.description:
“JavaScript Canvas Drawing to Server: Base64 vs Blob Upload Methods”

How can developers effectively capture user-generated drawings from an HTML <canvas> element and transmit this visual data to a server for permanent storage, considering options like Base64 encoding versus more efficient Blob manipulation?

The process involves several key steps: drawing the visual elements onto the canvas, serializing the canvas content into a transferable format, sending this data via an asynchronous request (like AJAX/Fetch) or a standard form submission, and finally, decoding and saving the resultant image file on the server-side.

item.title: JavaScript Canvas: Calculating Mouse Coordinates Across Scaling and Transformations
item.description:
“JavaScript Canvas: Calculating Mouse Coordinates Across Scaling and Transformations”

Obtaining precise mouse coordinates relative to an HTML <canvas> element is fundamental for interactive graphics programming. The complexity escalates when the element’s visual size (set by CSS) differs from its internal drawing buffer size (its width and height attributes), or when advanced canvas context transformations like rotation or scaling are applied. How can we reliably map screen coordinates to the canvas bitmap coordinates?
